issues.legal_issue: A final dismissal of a counterclaim that conclusively determines the counterclaimant’s rights is a decree that must be challenged by appeal, not set aside through supervisory jurisdiction.
material_facts: Defendants filed a counterclaim asserting rights under a will in a suit for a declaration of ownership and injunction.
The trial court finally dismissed the counterclaim as barred by the principles of Order 2, Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The High Court, exercising supervisory jurisdiction, set aside the trial court’s order.

The Supreme Court did not decide the merits of the dismissal or its reversal; it held that the trial court’s order had the status of a decree and could not be unsettled through supervisory jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The trial court’s final dismissal of the counterclaim was a decree, and it had to be challenged by appeal before the appropriate forum. The High Court could not set it aside in exercise of supervisory jurisdiction. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the counterclaimants were given liberty to appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 8, Rules 6A(2) and 6A(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a counterclaim has the effect of a cross-suit and is treated as a plaint; Rule 6D permits it to proceed even if the plaintiff’s suit is dismissed. When adjudication finally and conclusively determines the rights concerning the counterclaim, the resulting order satisfies the definition of a decree in Section 2(2) and is appealable. The Court relied on R. Rathinavel Chettiar v. V. Sivaraman, Jag Mohan Chawla v. Dera Radha Swami Satsang, and M/s. Ram Chand Spg. & Wvg. Mills v. M/s. Bijli Cotton Mills, which discussed when an adjudication conclusively determining rights has the status of a decree; the latter decision also referred to Jethanand and Sons v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Abdul Rahman v. D.K. Kassim and Sons. The Court held that supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 could not be used to unsettle the decree; it did not decide the merits of the counterclaim or the trial court’s reasoning.

predicates.counterclaim_case: A defendant asserted a claim against the plaintiff within an existing civil suit.
predicates.counterclaim_finally_dismissed: The court finally dismissed the defendant’s counterclaim rather than leaving it for later adjudication.
predicates.counterclaim_rights_conclusively_determi: The dismissal conclusively determined the rights asserted by the defendant in the counterclaim.
predicates.challenge_made_through_supervisory_juris: A party sought to set aside the dismissal through a higher court’s supervisory jurisdiction rather than by appeal.

issues.definition: When a defendant’s counterclaim in a civil suit is finally dismissed in a way that conclusively determines the counterclaim rights, a challenge made through supervisory jurisdiction must instead be brought by appeal.
